items.title: Benchmarking Language Model Creativity: A Case Study on Code Generation (NeoCoder; denial prompting; NAACL 2025)
items.quote: We introduce DENIAL PROMPTING which pushes LLMs to develop more creative solutions to a given problem by incrementally imposing new constraints on the previous solution, compelling LLMs to adopt new strategies.
items.relation: technique-level bans to elicit new strategies, scored behaviourally; no execution-order check of whether a banned technique returns under a new name

items.title: Compact Constraint Encoding for LLM Code Generation (Tang 2026)
items.quote: counter-intuitive constraints opposing model defaults fail at 10--100%, while conventional constraints achieve 99%+ compliance regardless of encoding.
items.relation: rule-based constraint compliance by constraint type (implementation priors); not mechanism-level vs name-level compliance

items.title: The Invisible Lottery: How Subtle Cues Steer Algorithm Choice in LLM Code Generation
items.quote: Incidental prompt cues, meaning contextual words or metadata outside the task specification, can steer which algorithm the model selects, even when all outputs pass the same tests.
items.relation: algorithm-family shifts under incidental cues; no prohibitions, no runtime expansion-order audit

items.title: Semantic Gravity Wells: Why Negative Constraints Backfire
items.quote: Negative constraints (instructions of the form "do not use word X") represent a fundamental test of instruction-following capability in large language models. Despite their apparent simplicity, these constraints fail with striking regularity
items.relation: word-level negative constraints and their internal suppression; ours are algorithm-level bans where the WORD can be avoided while the mechanism returns

items.title: Don't Think of the White Bear: Ironic Negation in Transformer Models Under Cognitive Load
items.quote: suppressing a concept requires internally activating it, which may prime rebound instead of avoidance.
items.relation: ironic rebound of a negated concept in text; ours measures rebound of a negated ALGORITHM in executed behaviour

items.title: IFEvalCode: Controlled Code Generation
items.quote: IFEvalCode decouples evaluation into two metrics: correctness (Corr.) and instruction-following (Instr.)
items.relation: programmatic checkers for code constraints incl. naming; a name checker cannot see a renamed mechanism, which is what the tracer adds

items.title: (query 7: specification gaming / renaming in code models)
items.relation: no scholarly or general hit studied lexical vs mechanistic compliance with algorithm bans; top hits were safety-bypass and peer-review gaming papers (results/positioning_raw/q7_*.txt)

permitted_wording_rule: the claim 'name-blind runtime audit shows bans are obeyed on names, not mechanisms' may be worded as new ONLY if N1-N3 hold (see results/headlines.json); otherwise only the descriptive measurement is reported
